Generalize the results of a test

Source: R/anon_generalize.R
anon_rule.Rd

Pairs an anon_quasi_values() specification with a rule, for anon_generalize(): the rule applies to every row of each test in the specification, and the test's other result columns are kept consistent with it.

Usage

anon_rule(spec, rule)

Arguments

spec

An anon_quasi_values() specification, such as the one given to anon_risk().

rule

A rule made by anon_band(), anon_round() or anon_fold().

Value

An object of class "anon_rule_values".

Details

The rule applies to the result_col of every row of each test, not only the row anon_risk() measures: any row identifies a subject as well as the baseline one. filter is not used here, for that reason.

When result_col is a numeric SDTM result (--STRESN) and the rule is a band or rounding, the text results of the same rows follow it:

  • --STRESC is rewritten from the generalized --STRESN;

  • --ORRES is rewritten from the generalized --STRESN: as it is where the units are the same (--ORRESU equals --STRESU), and otherwise times the row's own conversion factor (original --ORRES / original --STRESN), so it is never finer than --STRESN and unit conversion checks still pass. Without a factor (--STRESN missing or 0, or no unit columns and different values), it is blanked;

each in its own form (plain, with thousands separators such as "1,234", or in scientific notation such as "2.5E2") and with as many decimals as it had (in the same units, more where the generalized number needs them, such as a midpoint of 62.5 for "64"). Other results, such as "<5" or "ND", are left unchanged and counted in the log, with a warning where the row has a numeric result.

For ADaM, with result_col = "AVAL", AVALC is rewritten from the generalized AVAL, BASE is generalized by the same rule (it is the baseline AVAL) with BASEC rewritten from it, and CHG (AVAL - BASE), PCHG (100 * CHG / BASE) and R2BASE (AVAL / BASE) are recomputed from the generalized values. Where the generalized BASE is 0 (a band or rounding can make it so), PCHG and R2BASE become missing. Other derived columns (such as BASETYPE analyses, CRIT flags or AVALCAT) are not handled: generalize or remove them. Other result columns are generalized alone.

With anon_fold(), result_col must be text; on the rows folded, the other text results (--ORRES or --STRESC; AVALC, BASEC) become to too, and numeric ones become missing. Only the categories found in the test's rows count (a factor's levels are shared by every test).

See also

anon_generalize()

Examples

anon_rule(
  anon_quasi_values("vs", "VSTESTCD", c("HEIGHT", "WEIGHT"), "VSSTRESN"),
  anon_round(0)
)
#> <anon rule> anon_round(digits = 0) on `vs`: VSSTRESN where VSTESTCD is "HEIGHT", "WEIGHT" (every row)
